direction.text: Fazer reported record net sales of EUR 1,188.6 million for 2025 (2024: EUR 1,183.1 million); Confectionery reached an all-time high of EUR 580.6 million, while Bakery (EUR 446.9 million) and Lifestyle Foods (EUR 190.5 million) declined.

In July 2025 Fazer decided to invest approximately EUR 400 million in a new chocolate factory of about 33,300 m² in Lahti, Finland, due to start operating in 2028; chocolate production will partially continue in Vantaa.
At the end of 2025 Fazer had 4,693 employees (FTEs); 68% worked in Finland, 21% in Sweden and 10% in the Baltics.
In early 2025 Fazer completed moving production from its bakery in Kaunas, Lithuania, consolidating its Baltic bakery operations at its facility in Ogre, Latvia.
CEO Christoph Vitzthum said Fazer is pursuing growth not only organically but also through M&A; the company expects 2026 net sales to increase and comparable EBITDA to improve.

sustainability.text: Fazer reduced its Scope 1 and 2 emissions by 41% in 2025 compared with its 2020 baseline, citing actions such as replacing natural gas with electricity for steam production at its Lappeenranta confectionery factory and a new electric line at its Lahti bakery.
Fazer's Scope 3 emissions were 6% above the 2020 baseline in 2025; the company names limited supply-chain data as an obstacle and piloted product-level emission calculations for 100 SKUs.

Fazer targets a 50% cut in food loss by 2030 from 2020; in 2025 avoidable food loss fell 12% year on year and 24% against the 2020 baseline, and food loss is part of the Group's performance-based bonus scheme.
Fazer's Lost Time Accident Frequency was 2.7 in 2025 (2024: 4.0); it introduced Total Recordable Incident Frequency (11.9 in 2025) as a key safety indicator.
Fazer's Annual Report 2025, published 9 March 2026, includes a Business Review and a Sustainability Review alongside the financial statements.
The EU Omnibus I Directive, published in the Official Journal on 26 February 2026, limits CSRD reporting to EU companies with more than 1,000 employees and net turnover above EUR 450 million.

trends.text: Cocoa prices fell below USD 4,000 per tonne in February 2026, for the first time since November 2023, after record highs.
Citing higher raw-material and production costs, Fazer reduced several 200 g chocolate bars, including Fazer Blue, to 180 g from late August 2025, keeping recipes unchanged.

Fazer Lifestyle Foods' net sales fell to EUR 190.5 million in 2025 (2024: EUR 218.5 million), primarily due to lower B2B sales in Fazer's plant-based business; Fazer describes the plant-based drinks market as continuing to be challenging amid intense competition.

how_lindstrom_helps.why: Bakery, confectionery and factory staff (about 4,700 FTEs) need hygienic production workwear; a new Lahti factory from 2028 and consolidated Baltic production are natural points to review the workwear set-up.
Entrance and safety mats support hygiene and slip prevention at production sites, in line with Fazer's focus on lowering its lost-time accident frequency (LTAF) and recordable incidents.
Laundered cotton towel rolls instead of paper can support hand hygiene at food production sites and Fazer's stated goal of reducing value-chain (Scope 3) emissions.
